laocoon.geometryReviewNote: Complete historical straight-arm group, including its integral altar and low stepped base, without separate museum furniture. Full vertical extent runs from the underside of the base to the raised hand/serpent. The restored arm also controls the horizontal minimum, so neither the current Vatican height nor width applies to this cast. At H 242 cm the unchanged mesh measures about W 180.07 x D 106.89 cm in its current orientation. SMK records W 162.5 x D 103 cm and the Berlin master W 184 x D 100 cm; these disagree, so only the independently corroborated height calibrates the model and proportions are preserved.

identifiedObject.institution: Musei Capitolini, Rome - Palazzo dei Conservatori, Sale degli Horti Lamiani
identifiedObject.version_or_date: Second half of the 1st century BC (museum), found 1874 in the Horti Lamiani; the scan is a Geoffrey Marchal photogrammetry of a plaster cast in the SMK Royal Cast Collection (SMK cast accession not identified; Zenodo 10348289 / Sketchfab 544e56c1 could not be fetched)
identifiedObject.match_explanation: The catalogue note identifies the scan as Marchal's model of the SMK cast of the Esquiline Venus (Capitoline inv. 1141). The Esquiline Venus is a unique original; the identification of the cast/scan could not be re-verified because Zenodo (504) and Sketchfab (rate-limited) were unreachable.

roman/esquiline-venus-smk-cast.geometryReviewNote: The missing arms, tilted head, sandals, draped vase and cobra identify the Esquiline Venus. The official primary description explicitly places its feet on a quadrangular sculptural base and separately specifies the modern 81 × 60 × 40 cm display base. Three-angle inspection confirms the model includes the thin quadrangular sculptural foot but no modern display pedestal. The original sculpture's 155 cm surviving height therefore matches the whole modeled extent, as it does for the other Esquiline Venus route.
